From her time as an art student, she was known simply by her surname as she considered Dora to be "vulgar and sentimental". [ 1 ] She was not well known as a painter during her lifetime, as she rarely exhibited and did not sign her work. She worked for a while at the Omega Workshops , and for the Hogarth Press , designing woodcuts . [ 2 ] Early life [ edit ] Carrington was born in Hereford , England, to railway engineer Samuel Carrington, who worked for the East India Company , and Charlotte (née Houghton).
